<h3 id="intro">Introduction
      (<span class="Back"><a href="#start">Back to Beginning</a></span>) </h3>
  <p>
     This assignment consists of a single project for you to design and implement
     a significant piece of software on Unix systems using C.
  </p>
  <p>
    There are three projects for you to choose from. You are only required to
    complete one of the three projects. 
  </p>
  <p>
     Specific requirements of each project are given in the later sections 
     of this document. Your project selection is important, and in making 
     the selection the following should be considered:
   </p>
    <ol>
    <li> <p><strong>Project 1 - A Simple Unix Shell</strong></p>
        <p>The project  requires the use of more Unix systems facilities 
        and other functions than the other two projects. It also
        demands good C programming skills in designing the command line
        parser. Therefore the project is considered to be more difficult to
        implement than the other two and this will be taken into consideration
        during assessment. A lot can be learnt about operating systems  by
        doing this project. 
        </p>
    </li>
    <li><p><strong>Project 2 - A Simple File Transfer Protocol</strong></p>
       <p>The project requires three pieces of work: a network protocol
         specification, a client program that implements the client 
         side of the protocol,  and a server program that implements 
         the server side of the protocol. As beginners in network
         programming,  most students tend to 
         overlook the importance of correct protocol design and 
         specification. They often write a "protocol" after they 
         have written up the client and the server programs. 
         This is like hiring an architecture to draw up a blue print 
         for a new  palace after the palace is already built. Correct 
         specification of the communication protocol is required in
         this project,  and you can 
         expect to lose many marks if your protocol specification is 
         not complete or correct or not corresponding to what you 
         have implemented! Having said that,  programming wise, it is
         relatively straightforward to implement the code once the
         network protocol is correctly specified.
       </p>
    </li>
    <li><p><strong>Project 3 - A Simple HTTP Client and Server </strong></p>
       <p>This project is similar to Project 2 in some aspects. 
        However it requires you to learn a non-trivial, <em>existing</em> 
        network protocol, HTTP, and to thoroughly understand it, 
        at least in the parts that are required by this project. 
        Therefore you will need to make a lot of efforts to conduct 
        an independent research and self-learning before you can even 
        start to write a single line of code. Once you understand the 
        protocol it is not too difficult (but can be tedious) 
        to write a client and a server that is logically sound but 
        inefficient.  However, it is a challenge to design and implement 
        an HTTP client and an HTTP server that are both correct to 
        the protocol specification and also  efficient!
        </p>
    </li>
    </ol>
  <p>Alternatively you may propose your own project.  However it must 
     have similar level of technical contents and be of a similar 
     level of technical difficulty. The project must be approved by 
     the Unit Coordinator. 
     If you intend to do your own project you should discuss it with 
     your Unit Coordinator as early as is possible.  
  </p>
  <p>
     The project will be marked out of 100 marks, of which 10% is attributed
     to compliance to the <a href="#docs"> Documentation Requirements</a>.  
     To achieve good marks you must strictly adhere to the <a href="#docs"> 
     Documentation Requirements</a>.
  </p>
   <p class="Emphasize"> 
     In presenting your work, you must document the test cases and test 
     outputs for each feature required by the project. The test output 
     can be in the form of terminal output. You may copy the text from
     the terminal output and paste it to your Word document 
     (always include the command line). You should format 
     the terminal output using a monospaced font so that it is 
     clearly distinguishable from the rest of texts in your document.
     It is even better if you place the terminal output in a text box 
     so that it is clearly separated from other texts in your document. 
     But do not modify your test output unless it is too long and 
     repetitive - heavy penalties will be applied if test output is 
     modified to make your work appear better than what it really is!  
   </p>
   <p class="Emphasize"> 
     Marking will be based on the number of working features demonstrated
     in your documentation. If a feature works and <em> you have provided 
     test evidence </em> that the feature works in the form of test cases 
     and test outputs, and your explanation of the test is convincing,
     you will get the marks allocated to the feature.  Otherwise you 
     will not get marks for that feature even if you have implemented it. 
   </p>
   <p class="Emphasize"> 
     Read <a href="#docs">Documentation Requirements</a> for further 
     and more detailed requirements regarding the test documentation. 
   </p>
   <p> 
     The project requires a significant amount of work on design and 
     implementation. It is advised that you should start the project
     as soon as possible. 
  </p>

  <h3 id="deadline">Deadline and Penalty for Late Submission 
      (<span class="Back"><a href="#start">Back to Beginning</a></span>) </h3>

  <p>
     The submission deadline of this assignment is specified in
     ICT310 Teaching Schedule page of <a href="../../index.html">
      the Unit Website</a>.
  </p>
  <p>
     Assignments  submitted on or before the deadline will be 
     marked out of 100%. 
  </p>
  <p> Late submission of the assignment will have 5% of the student's raw 
      mark deducted per day, unless an application for extension of submission
      deadline is granted. A submission that is late by more than 10 days 
      or after the last teaching week (Week 14) will not be accepted. 
  </p>
   <p>
     Applications for extension of your assignment deadline can only be made
     via email to the Unit Coordinator, normally prior to
     the specified due date of the assignment.  If an extension is granted
     (also by email), you must attach a copy of the email to your submission
     (see <a href="#docs">Documentation Requirements</a>). Applications 
     for extension by phone or in person do not count,  even if granted.  
     The above policy will be rigorously enforced.
   </p>

  <h3 id="p1"> Project 1: A Simple Unix Shell
      (<span class="Back"><a href="#start">Back to Beginning</a></span>) </h3>
    <p>
       Design and implement a simple UNIX shell program using the grammar
       specified in the <a href="#syntax">later part</a> of this section.
       Please allow for at least 100 commands in a command line and at 
       least 1000 arguments in each command.
    </p>
    <p>
       In addition to the above, the following are required:
     </p>
       <ol>
       <li> <p class="Emphasize"> Reconfigurable shell prompt (default %)</p>  
            <p> The shell must have a shell built-in command <tt>prompt</tt> 
                for changing  the current prompt.  For example, type the 
                following command
            </p>
<pre>
% prompt john$
</pre>
            <p>
                should change the shell prompt to <tt>john$</tt>, i.e., the 
                second  token of the command.
            </p>
       </li>
       <li> <p class="Emphasize">The shell built-in command <code>pwd</code> </p>
            <p> This command prints the current directory (also known as 
                <em>working directory</em>) of the shell process.
            </p>
       </li> 
       <li> <p class="Emphasize">Directory walk</p>
            <p>This command is similar to that provided by the 
               Bash built-in command <tt>cd</tt>. In particular, typing 
               the command without a path should set the current directory 
               of the shell to the home directory of the user.
            </p>
       </li>
       <li> <p class="Emphasize">Wildcard characters</p>
            <p>If a token contains wildcard characters <code>*</code> 
               or <code>?</code> the token is treated as a filename. 
               The wildcard characters in such a token indicate to the 
               shell that the filename must be expanded.  For example 
               the command
            </p>
<pre>
% ls *.c
</pre>
           <p>
               may be expanded to <code>ls ex1.c ex2.c ex3.c </code>if there 
               are three matching files <code>ex1.c ex2.c ex3.c </code> in 
               the current directory.
            </p>
            <p> You may implement this feature using the C function 
               <code>glob</code>.
            </p>
       </li>
       <li> <p class="Emphasize">Standard input and output redirections &gt; and &lt;</p>
            <p> For example:
            </p>
<pre>
% ls -lt &gt;  foo
</pre>
           <p>
               would redirect the standard output of process 
               <tt>ls -lt</tt> to file <tt>foo</tt>.  Similarly in the 
               following command,
            </p>
<pre>
% cat &lt;  foo
</pre>
           <p>
               the standard input of process <tt>cat</tt> is redirected 
               to file <tt>foo</tt>.
            </p>
       </li>
       <li> <p class="Emphasize">Shell pipeline |</p>
           <p>For example: </p>
<pre>
% ls -lt | more
</pre>
         <p>
              the standard output of process <tt>ls -lt</tt>  is connected 
              to the standard input of process <tt>more</tt> via a pipe.
           </p>
       </li>
       <li> <p class="Emphasize">Background job execution</p>
            <p> For example: </p>
<pre>
% xterm &amp;
</pre>
         <p>
               The commannd line starts command <tt>xterm</tt> in the 
               background (ie the shell will not wait for it to terminate
               and you can type in the next command immediately). 
               The following command line
         </p>
<pre>
% sleep 20 &amp;  ps -l
</pre>
         <p>
              starts command  <tt>sleep 20</tt> and immediately execute 
              command <tt>ps -l</tt> without waiting for command 
              <tt>sleep 20</tt> to finish first.
           </p>
       </li>
       <li> <p class="Emphasize">Sequential job execution</p>
            <p> For example the command line
           </p>
<pre>
%  sleep 20 ; ps -l
</pre>
           <p>
               starts command <tt>sleep 20</tt> first, and wait for it 
               to finish, then execute command <tt>ps -l</tt>.
            </p>
       </li>
       <li> <p class="Emphasize">The shell built-in command <code>exit </code></p>
            <p> Use the built-in command <code>exit</code> to terminate
                the shell program.
            </p>
       </li>
       </ol>
      <p> Finally you must not use any existing shell program to 
          implement your shell (for example by calling a shell through 
          the function <code>system</code>).  That would defeat the purpose 
          of this project.
      </p>
      <p> In the above, commands such as <tt>ls</tt>, <tt>cat</tt>, 
          <tt> grep</tt>, <tt>sleep</tt>, <tt>ps</tt> and <tt>xterm</tt>  
          are used as examples to illustrate the use of 
          your shell program. However your shell must be able to handle
          <em>any</em> command or executable program. Note the  commands 
          <tt>prompt</tt>, <tt>pwd</tt>, <tt>cd</tt> and <tt>exit</tt> should be  
          implemented as shell builtins, not as external commands.
      </p>
      <p> The syntax and behaviour of the built-in commands 
          <tt>pwd</tt>, <tt>cd</tt> and <tt> exit</tt> should be similar to the 
          corresponding commands under Bash shell. 
      </p>
      <p> A major part of this shell is a command line parser. 
          Please read the <a href="shell_notes.shtml">this note</a>
          for suggestions on implementing the parser.
      </p>

    <h4 id="syntax"> Definition of Command Line Syntax </h4>
      <p>The following is the formal definition of the command line 
         syntax for the shell, defined in Extended BNF:
      </p>
<pre>
   &lt; command line &gt;      ::=   &lt; job &gt;
                             | &lt; job &gt; '&amp;'
                             | &lt; job &gt; '&amp;' &lt; command line &gt;
                             | &lt; job &gt; ';'
                             | &lt; job &gt; ';' &lt; command line &gt;

   &lt; job &gt;               ::=   &lt; command &gt;
                             | &lt; job &gt; '|' &lt; command &gt;

   &lt; command &gt;           ::=   &lt; simple command &gt;
                             | &lt; simple command &gt; '&lt;' &lt; filename &gt;
                             | &lt; simple command &gt; '&gt;' &lt; filename &gt;

   &lt; simple command &gt;    ::=   &lt; pathname &gt;
                             | &lt; simple command &gt;  &lt; token &gt;
</pre>
      <p>An informal definition plus additional explanations of the 
         syntax is given below: 
        </p>
         <ol>
         <li> <p>A <span class="Emphasize">command line</span>  consists of one 
              or several <span class="Emphasize">jobs</span> separated by the 
              special character "&amp;" and/or ";".  The last <span class="Emphasize">
              job</span> may be followed by the character "&amp;" 
              or ";". If a <span class="Emphasize">job</span> is followed by 
              the character "&amp;", then it should  be executed in background.  
             </p>
         </li>
         <li> <p>A <span class="Emphasize">job</span>  consists of one or more
              <span class="Emphasize">command</span>s separated by pipeline
              characters "|"; 
              </p>
         </li>
         <li> <p>A <span class="Emphasize">command</span> is either a 
              <span class="Emphasize">simple command</span> or a <span class="Emphasize">
              simple command</span> followed by an input redirection
              (&lt; filename) or an output redirection (&gt; filename); 
             </p>
         </li>
         <li> <p>A <span class="Emphasize">simple command</span> consists of a single
              <span class="Emphasize">pathname</span> followed by zero or more tokens; 
              </p>
         </li>
         <li> <p>The following five characters are the <span class="Emphasize">special 
              characters</span>: &amp;, ;, |, &lt; , &gt; ; 
              </p>
         </li>
         <li> <p>The <span class="Emphasize">white space characters</span> are 
              defined to be the space character and the tab character; 
              </p>
         </li>
         <li><p>A <span class="Emphasize">token</span> is either a special character 
              or a string that does not contain space characters or 
              special characters. In this project we do not consider 
              quoted strings. Therefore if single quote or double quote 
              characters appear in a string, they are treated just like 
              any other non-special characters without the usually special
              meaning;
              </p>
         </li>
         <li> <p><span class="Emphasize">Tokens</span> must be separated by one 
              or more white spaces; 
              </p>
         </li>
         <li><p>A <span class="Emphasize">pathname</span> is either a file name, 
             or an absolute pathname, or a relative pathname. Examples of 
             pathnames are <strong>grep</strong>, <strong>/usr/bin/grep</strong>,
             <strong>bin/grep</strong> and <strong>./grep</strong>; 
             </p>
         </li>
         <li> <p>A command line must end with a newline character.
              </p>
         </li>
         </ol>

  <h3 id="p2"> Project 2: A Simple File Transfer Protocol 
      (<span class="Back"><a href="#start">Back to Beginning</a></span>) </h3>
     <p>
        Design and implement a simple network protocol that can be used to
        download files from a remote site and to upload files to a remote
        site, and a client and a server programs that communicate using 
        that protocol.  The protocol should use TCP as its transport 
        layer protocol.  The server must be able to serve multiple client 
        requests simultaneously.  For simplicity, do not consider any 
        authentication process in this project, hence the server will 
        provide its service to any client with the right site address 
        and port number.
     </p>
     <p>
        To simplify project marking, please name your server program
        <tt>myftpd</tt> with the following command line syntax (here the
        letter <tt>d</tt> in <tt>myftpd</tt> stands for daemon, since the 
        server should run as a daemon process:
     </p>
<pre>
myftpd [ initial_current_directory ]
</pre>
     <p>
        The server process maintains a current directory. Its initial
        value should be the one inherited from its parent process
        unless the optional
     </p>
<pre>
initial_current_directory
</pre>
     <p>
        is given. In the latter case, the user supplied path should be
        used to set the initial current directory of the server.
        This can be done using the function <code>chdir</code>.  A client
        can use the <code>cd</code> command to change the (child) server's
        current directory later.
      </p>
      <p>
        The client program should be named <tt>myftp</tt> with the 
        following command line syntax:
      </p>
<pre>
myftp [ hostname | IP_address ]
</pre>
     <p>
        where the optional <tt><i>hostname</i></tt> 
        (<tt><i>IP_address</i></tt>) is the name (address) of the remote 
        host that provides the <tt>myftp</tt> service. If the 
        <tt><i>hostname</i></tt> or <tt><i>IP_address</i></tt> is omitted,
        the local host is assumed.
     </p>
     <p>
        After the connection between the client and the server is
        established, the client should display a prompt <tt>&gt;</tt> 
        and wait for one of the following commands:
     </p>
<ul>
<li> <p><code>pwd</code> - to display the  current directory of the 
        server that is serving the client; </p></li>
<li> <p><code>lpwd</code> - to display the  current directory of 
        the client; </p></li> 
<li> <p><code>dir</code> - to display the file names under the  current 
       directory of the server that is serving the client; </p></li>
<li> <p><code>ldir</code> - to display the file names under the  current 
       directory of the client; </p></li>
<li> <p><code>cd directory_pathname</code>  - to change the current directory
      of the server that is serving the client;</p> </li>
<li> <p><code>lcd directory_pathname</code>  - to change the current directory
      of the client;</p> </li>
<li> <p> <code>get filename </code> - to download the named file from the
       current directory of the  remote server and save
       it in the current directory of the client;</p> </li>
<li> <p> <code>put filename </code> - to upload the named file from the
      current directory of the client to the current
      directory of the remove server. </p> </li>
<li> <p> <code> quit </code> - to terminate the <code> myftp</code> session.</p></li>
</ul>
    <p>
       The <tt>myftp</tt> client should repeatedly display the prompt 
       and wait for a command until the <tt> quit</tt> command is entered.
    </p>
    <p>
      This project consists of three components:
     </p>
<ol>
<li> <p class="Emphasize">Protocol Specification:</p>
     <p> You must specify 
     a protocol for communication between the <tt>myftp</tt> 
     client and the <tt>myftp</tt> server. This protocol will 
     become the <em>sole</em> reference to which the client program 
     and the server program can be separately implemented.  
     This means that, by referring
     to the protocol, the client and server can be implemented
     independent of each other. The design and implementation of
     the client (server) should not depend on (1) what
     strategy and algorithms were used to implement the server
     (client), (2) what programming language were used to implement
     the server (client), and (3) what operating system the server (client)
     is running on. The protocol must be complete,
     i.e.,  it contains all the necessary information required by
     both parties to communicate, such as the format and sequence
     of data exchanges between the client and the server, the
     transport layer protocol (TCP or UDP) used to deliver the
     data, and the server port number.  However it should not
     contain anything that unnecessarily constrains the implementation
     of the client or the server.  For example, there is no point
     to limit the implementation language to a particular programming
     language in the protocol, or to require the client or the server
     to be implemented with a particular data structure.
     </p>
     <p>
     Before you attempt this project, you should first complete 
     the first two exercises in Lab 11. You may also read 
     the Trivial FTP Protocol given in Appendix 17A of the textbook 
     (Stallings: Chapter 17 of Online Chapters). Note TFTP uses UDP, while  
      <tt>myftp</tt> protocol must use TCP.
     </p>
</li>
<li> <p class="Emphasize">Client Program:</p>
     <p>You need to implement a client program according to
     the <tt> myftp</tt> protocol.  Note that the client should 
     never rely on any undocumented internal tricks in the server
     implementation. Apart from the <tt>myftp</tt>  protocol,
     you should not make any other assumption about the server 
     program in your client program.
     </p>
</li>
<li> <p class="Emphasize"> Server Program:</p>
     <p> You need to  implement a server program according to
      the <tt> myftp</tt> protocol.  Note that the server 
      should never rely on any undocumented internal tricks 
      in the client implementation. Apart from the <tt>myftp</tt> 
      protocol,  you should not make any other assumption about 
      the client program in your server program.
    </p>
</li>
</ol>

  <p>Note the following additional requirements/explanations:</p>

<ul>
<li>  <p>The name of the client executable program must be <tt>myftp</tt>.
      The name of the server executable program must be <tt>myftpd</tt>.
      </p>
</li>
<li>  <p> To avoid potential conflict in the use of the server's 
      ``well known'' port number when  several students 
      use the same machine (such as medusa), you should use the 
      <a href="server_ports.pdf"> port </a> allocated to you as the default server listening port.
      </p>
</li>
<li>  <p>Tests should show the cases where both the client and the
      server are on the same machine as well as on different
      machines (you may want to use medusa.murdoch.edu.au to do 
      the testing, however <span class="Emphasize">you must kill your server at 
      the end of the test</span>). They should also show that more
      than one client can obtain the service at the same time.
      You may use the command <tt>script</tt> to record the 
      terminal I/O.  When debugging your network program on 
      a standalone machine (eg, on your home Linux), you may 
      use <tt>localhost</tt> as the ``remote'' host name.
      </p>
</li>
<li>  <p>The specification of the protocol is an important part of
      this question.  Please provide a full specification of the
      protocol in a section separated from the client and server
      implementations. You should complete this specification 
      before starting the implementation of the client and 
      server programs.
      </p>
</li>
</ul>

  <h3 id="p3"> Project 3: A HTTP Client and an HTTP Server 
      (<span class="Back"><a href="#start">Back to Beginning</a></span>) </h3>
     <p>
       This project involves an independent study of an existing 
       protocol named HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol), 
       version 1.0 and version 1.1, and then 
       design and Implement an HTTP client that is able to 
       communicate with any HTTP server, and design and implement
       an HTTP server that is able to provide simple services
       requested by any HTTP client.
     </p>
     <p>Please note that a thorough understanding of the HTTP protocol is
       an important part of this project. Unless you are confident that 
       you are  able to gain a thorough understanding of the protocol, 
       you should not select this project as your assignment.
     </p>
     <p>
       This project has three components:
       </p>
       <ol>
         <li>An essay of between one to two pages long, explaining 
             your understanding of the HTTP protocol.
         </li>
         <li> Design and implementation of an HTTP client program using C,
              see the detailed requirements below.
         </li>
         <li> Design and implementation of an HTTP server program using C, 
              see the detailed requirements below.
         </li>
       </ol>

      <h4>The HTTP Client</h4>
      <p>
         The client program must be able to request resources using 
         the GET method from any HTTP server, such as Apache,
         Microsoft IISi and your own HTTP server. It must also be able
         to handle HEAD and TRACE methods. However it is not required to
         render HTML or any graphics or to manipulate HTML links. 
         Content from an HTTP server can be displayed in the same format 
         as you receive it on the terminal.
      </p>
      <p>
          The client should  be named <tt>myhttp</tt> with the following 
          command line syntax: 
      </p>
<pre>
    myhttp [ -m  <i>&lt;method &gt;</i>  [ -a ]  <i>&lt;url&gt;</i>
</pre>
     <p>
       The command takes an url and send an HTTP request message to 
       the server and receives the response from the server. If there
       is no <tt> -a</tt> option, the program displays the content of
       the response. Otherwise it displays entire response message including
       both the headers and the content. 
      </p>
      <p>By default, the client uses GET method. But if the command line
        include an <tt>-m</tt> option, the client should either use
        HEAD method or TRACE method: If the option is <tt>-m head</tt>, 
        the client should use HEAD method; If the option is <tt>-m trace</tt>, 
        the client should use TRACE method.
      </p>

      <h4>The HTTP Server</h4>

      <p> The server program must be able to perform the following tasks:
        </p>
         <ul>
            <li> serve files or directory listings in response to GET 
                 requests from any HTTP client, such as Mozilla Firefox, 
                 Microsoft Internet as well as your own HTTP client.
            </li>
            <li> handle HEAD method and TRACE method from any client.
            </li> 
            <li> input a MIME type file containing a list of MIME type
                  definition and handle the content accordingly.
            </li>
         </ul>
       <p>
       In addition, your server should run as a daemon and it should 
       be able to serve multiple client requests simultaneously.  
       The server should  be named <tt>myhttpd</tt> with the following 
       command line syntax: 
       </p>
<pre>
    myhttpd [ -p  <i>&lt;port number&gt;</i> ]
            [ -d  <i>&lt;document root&gt;</i> ]
            [ -l  <i>&lt;log file&gt;</i> ]
            [ -m  <i>&lt;file for mime types&gt;</i> ]
            [ -f  <i>&lt;number of preforks&gt;</i> ]
</pre>
      <p> where  </p>
       <ul>
       <li> <p><tt><i>&lt;port number&gt;</i></tt> is an optional port 
            number for the server.  If the optional port number is not 
            supplied, your server should use TCP port 8000. 
            </p>
            <p>
               The default port for HTTP is TCP 80. However on Unix, 
               only the root can use ports that are below 1024. 
               To run your server with port 80, you must logon as the 
               root (which is not possible in some machines such as
               medusa.murdoch.edu.au). This is the reason we use 
               port 8000 instead of 80 as the default port.
            </p>
            <p>When testing your server on a shared machine such as
               medusa, you should avoid using port 8000, as there may
               be clashes if two students use the same port at the same 
               time on that machine.  To avoid potential conflict 
               you should use the <a href="server_ports.pdf"> port </a> 
               allocated to you to test your server.
            </p></li>
       <li> <p><tt><i>&lt;document root&gt;</i></tt> is an optional
            directory path representing the document root of the server
            under which all files are stored. Without this option, 
            you document root is taken as the current directory of the
            server.
            </p>
            <p> When testing your server, make sure that under your
               document root, there are regular files as well as 
               directories. Some of these directories contains 
               the index file <tt>index.html</tt>. Other directories 
               do not contain this index file.  Your should test 
               both cases.
            </p></li> 
       <li> <p><tt><i>&lt;log file&gt;</i></tt> is an optional path of
            the log file, to which the server will send its logs. 
            Without this option, your log file should be 
            <tt>./myhttdp.log</tt>, ie file <tt>myhttpd.log</tt> 
            under the server's current directory.
            </p>
            <p>Your server must add one line into the log file for 
               each client request, giving the date and time of the 
               request, the HTTP method in the request, the originating 
               host, the resource request and status code returned
               to the client.
            </p></li> 
       <li> <p><tt><i>&lt;file for mime types&gt;</i></tt> is an optional
            file containing a list of mime types that the server 
            recognises. Without this option, your server would only
            recognise the following mime types:
               <tt>text/plain</tt>, <tt>text/html</tt>, <tt>image/jpeg</tt>, 
               and <tt>image/gif</tt>. 
            </p>
            <p>In testing your server, you must at least test the above
               file types plus two additional file types.
            </p></li>
       <li> <p><tt><i>&lt;number of preforks&gt;</i></tt> is an optional
            number of preforks. Without this option, the number of
            preforks is fixed at 5. 
            </p>
            <p>Preforks mean that the server
            (parent server) will always maintain a pool of idle child 
            processes (child servers), so that when a client request 
            arrives, the parent server can immediately hand it to one 
            of the idle child servers. In this way the client can get 
            speedier service rather than waiting for the parent server 
            to create a new child process before it can be served. 
            Note that it takes a long time to create new  child process.
            </p>
            <p>It is not a trivial task to design an efficient web server 
               that can serve many client requests simultaneously and 
               quickly. You may want to consider using <tt>clone</tt>
               systems call to create child processes to reduce the 
               overhead. However if you choose to do so, you must be
               careful with the global variables as they are shared 
               between the parent and all child processes! 
            </p></li>
       </ul>
       <p>Please note that the server <tt>myhttpd</tt> can take any combination
          of the above five command line options, not necessarily one option
          each time. For example, we may run the server with two options
          as shown below:
       </p>
<pre>
%  myhttpd  -p 12345  -l /tmp/hong.log
</pre>
       <p>In addition to the above requirements, your server must be able
          list file names in a directory if the URL points to a directory
          on the server and that directory does not contain an index file
          (<tt>index.html</tt>).
       </p>
       <p>
         To complete this project you will have to carry out research on
         issues such as web server, HTTP protocol, MIME type, etc.  
         There are numerous Internet sites providing the 
         relevant materials.  A good starting point is 
         <a href="http://en.wikipedia.org">Wikipedia</a>.
       </p>

<h3 id="docs"> Documentation Requirements 
      (<span class="Back"><a href="#start">Back to Beginning</a></span>) </h3>
     <p>
         Your assignment must be submitted in the form of a single tar 
         archive file via the Unit LMS. The tar file must be 
         named in the following format:
     </p>
<pre>
       A2_&lt;your family name&gt;_&lt;your first name&gt;.tar
</pre>
     <p>
      For example, the student, John Smith, would name his tar file as:
      <tt>A2_Smith_John.tar</tt>.
     </p>
     <p>
      Your tar archive must contain the following files:
      </p>
      <ul>
          <li> <p>
               One Microsoft Word document named "Assignment2.doc". This 
               file replaces the hard-copy submission that is 
               required in the traditional non-electronic submissions. 
               See the detailed requirements of this file later
               in this section.  
              </p>
          </li>
          <li> <p>
               All your C/C++source code, makefiles used to compile source
               code and to build the executable programs, Linux executable
               programs, test files, test output files, etc,  
               that are related to your project.
              </p>
          </li>  
        </ul>
      <p> You can create test output files by cut-and-pasting from 
          your terminal output into a text file. 
          Alternatively you may use command <tt>script</tt> to record 
          terminal input and output (but you need to remove the control
          characters). Please do not modify the test
          output.
      </p>
      <p> You must make sure that your program can be compiled and run
          in other machines. Do not use any non-standard feature or
          any feature that is only available in your machine. 
          Do not hard code any directory path into your program otherwise
          your program may not run on someone else's machine. 
       </p>
  
      <h4> The file "Assignment2.doc" </h4>
     <p>
       This Word file should contain the documents in the following order:
      </p>
       <ol>
          <li><p class="Emphasize">Assignment Declaration:</p>
              <p> all students (internal and external) must complete 
                  <a href="ICT310AssignmentTwoDeclarationForm.doc">
                  ICT310 Assignment Two Declaration Form</a> and this form 
                  and include it in your Word file. 
               </p>
          </li> 
          <li><p class="Emphasize">Extension Granted:</p>
              <p> If you have been granted extension, include the email 
                  from your Unit Coordinator after the declaration form.
                  The extension does not count unless it is documented here.
              </p>
          </li>
           <li>
             <p class="Emphasize">List of Files:</p>
                <p>  List the name and purpose of each file 
                included in the tar archive.
             </p>
           </li>
           <li> 
             <p class="Emphasize">The project title and a brief description 
                of the project:</p>
             <p>  You can cut-and-paste the project question from this web 
                     page to your Word file.  </p>
           </li>
           <li><p class="Emphasize">Self diagnosis:</p>
                <p> Provide  a statement giving </p>
               <ol>
               <li> <p> a list of features that are fully functional. 
                    </p>
               </li>
               <li> <p> a list of features that are not fully functional
                     (include features that are not fully implemented, or 
                      not implemented at all).
                    </p>
                </li>
                </ol>
               <p>
               This statement is essential. There will be penalty  
               if this statement is too vague or short of details.  
               Heavy penalty will be applied if this statement is misleading.
               </p>
           </li>
           <li> <p class="Emphasize">Test eveidence:</p>
              <p> You must provide sufficient number of test cases to demonstrate 
               and convince your tutor that your project has met all requirements.
              </p>
              <p>
                For each test case, you should 1) explain the purpose of the test, 
                2) provide the test output including the command line used, 
                and 3) give an explanation on what the test has achieved based on 
                the test results.
              </p>
              <p> It is important that you present a sufficient number of test cases 
                to convince your tutor that your solution works in all situations. 
                Please note that although your tutor may test your program to verify 
                the evidence presented in your documentation, it is not the 
                responsibility of your tutor to test your program for the purpose of 
                finding marks for you. It is up to individual student to mount a 
                convincing case that the submitted solution works as required. You will 
                be be awarded marks based on the test evicences you have presented. 
                Therefore if you do not provide test evidence you do not get marks 
                regardless of whether your program works or not, or if the test 
                evidence you have provided is not sufficient, your marks will be
                substantially reduced.
              </p>
              <p> You should format your test output using fonts such as courier 
                so that test output is clearly distinguishable from the rest of the 
                document. You should not modify the test output unless it is too 
                long and repetitive.
              </p>
              <p> In presenting your test cases, do not use the tabular format that 
                you may have been told to use in some other units. Simply present one 
                test case after the other in a linear order.
              </p>
            </li>
           <li> <p class="Emphasize"> Source code listing: </p> 
                <p> The source code must be properly indented, commented, 
                    and formatted. The source code included in this Word 
                    file must be identical to that of source code files 
                    included in the tar archive. 
                </p>
                <p> You must also include the makefile for building your program.
                </p>
           </li>
       </ol>
      <p>
         Your tutor will mark your project directly on your Word file. 
         The marked project with comments will be returned to you via Unit LMS. 
       </p>
      <p class="Emphasize">
          The documentation requirements,  as described above, will be strictly enforced.
          Your project will not be marked, or your marks will be significantly
          reduced, if you fail to adhere to the above requirements.
       </p>

<h3 id="policy"> Policy on the Reuse of the Third Party Source Code
      (<span class="Back"><a href="#start">Back to Beginning</a></span>) </h3>

 <p> Please read this section very carefully.
 </p>

<p>All students are encouraged to solve the problems independently with
their own source code. I understand, however, that occasionally there
may be justifiable reasons to re-use source code from a third party.
Please note that if you have used one or more pieces of third party source
code in your program (this includes the situations where you have made
minor modifications to the third party source code), your project 
will be acceptable only if you have satisfied all of the following
conditions:
</p>

<ul>
<li> The third party source code is fully identified, including the page
numbers and line numbers in your hard-copy project documentation, and</li>

<li> The origin of the third party code is fully disclosed and acknowledged
in your project submission, and</li>

<li> The third party source code is fully commented in your program listing.
All variables, functions and major control structures must be commented to
show clearly that you understand the logic of the code, and </li>

<li>The third party source code is less than 20% of your program
(in terms of the number of lines), excluding the code specifically allowed
to be used.</li>

</ul>

<p>Failure to satisfy any one of the above conditions will result in
0 marks being awarded to your entire project. </p>

<p>The above policy will be rigorously enforced by the Unit Coordinator
and Tutors. </p>

<h3 id="grievance">Grievance with Assignment Marking
      (<span class="Back"><a href="#start">Back to Beginning</a></span>) </h3>
  <p>
       Once you have received your marked assignment, if you have any grievance
       with the marking, you must raise it with your Unit Coordinator by email,
       within 7 days of returning of your marked assignment to the Unit LMS,
       or within the announced deadline in the Unit Website, whichever is earlier.
       Otherwise the marks awarded to you will be final and will be used to calculate
       your final weighted average score for the unit.
   </p>

<h3 id="intro">Introduction
      (<span class="Back"><a href="#start">Back to Beginning</a></span>) </h3>
  <p>
     This assignment consists of a single project for you to design and implement
     a significant piece of software on Unix systems using C.
  </p>
  <p>
    There are three projects for you to choose from. You are only required to
    complete one of the three projects. 
  </p>
  <p>
     Specific requirements of each project are given in the later sections 
     of this document. Your project selection is important, and in making 
     the selection the following should be considered:
   </p>
    <ol>
    <li> <p><strong>Project 1 - A Simple Unix Shell</strong></p>
        <p>The project  requires the use of more Unix systems facilities 
        and other functions than the other two projects. It also
        demands good C programming skills in designing the command line
        parser. Therefore the project is considered to be more difficult to
        implement than the other two and this will be taken into consideration
        during assessment. A lot can be learnt about operating systems  by
        doing this project. 
        </p>
    </li>
    <li><p><strong>Project 2 - A Simple File Transfer Protocol</strong></p>
       <p>The project requires three pieces of work: a network protocol
         specification, a client program that implements the client 
         side of the protocol,  and a server program that implements 
         the server side of the protocol. As beginners in network
         programming,  most students tend to 
         overlook the importance of correct protocol design and 
         specification. They often write a "protocol" after they 
         have written up the client and the server programs. 
         This is like hiring an architecture to draw up a blue print 
         for a new  palace after the palace is already built. Correct 
         specification of the communication protocol is required in
         this project,  and you can 
         expect to lose many marks if your protocol specification is 
         not complete or correct or not corresponding to what you 
         have implemented! Having said that,  programming wise, it is
         relatively straightforward to implement the code once the
         network protocol is correctly specified.
       </p>
    </li>
    <li><p><strong>Project 3 - A Simple HTTP Client and Server </strong></p>
       <p>This project is similar to Project 2 in some aspects. 
        However it requires you to learn a non-trivial, <em>existing</em> 
        network protocol, HTTP, and to thoroughly understand it, 
        at least in the parts that are required by this project. 
        Therefore you will need to make a lot of efforts to conduct 
        an independent research and self-learning before you can even 
        start to write a single line of code. Once you understand the 
        protocol it is not too difficult (but can be tedious) 
        to write a client and a server that is logically sound but 
        inefficient.  However, it is a challenge to design and implement 
        an HTTP client and an HTTP server that are both correct to 
        the protocol specification and also  efficient!
        </p>
    </li>
    </ol>
  <p>Alternatively you may propose your own project.  However it must 
     have similar level of technical contents and be of a similar 
     level of technical difficulty. The project must be approved by 
     the Unit Coordinator. 
     If you intend to do your own project you should discuss it with 
     your Unit Coordinator as early as is possible.  
  </p>
  <p>
     The project will be marked out of 100 marks, of which 10% is attributed
     to compliance to the <a href="#docs"> Documentation Requirements</a>.  
     To achieve good marks you must strictly adhere to the <a href="#docs"> 
     Documentation Requirements</a>.
  </p>
   <p class="Emphasize"> 
     In presenting your work, you must document the test cases and test 
     outputs for each feature required by the project. The test output 
     can be in the form of terminal output. You may copy the text from
     the terminal output and paste it to your Word document 
     (always include the command line). You should format 
     the terminal output using a monospaced font so that it is 
     clearly distinguishable from the rest of texts in your document.
     It is even better if you place the terminal output in a text box 
     so that it is clearly separated from other texts in your document. 
     But do not modify your test output unless it is too long and 
     repetitive - heavy penalties will be applied if test output is 
     modified to make your work appear better than what it really is!  
   </p>
   <p class="Emphasize"> 
     Marking will be based on the number of working features demonstrated
     in your documentation. If a feature works and <em> you have provided 
     test evidence </em> that the feature works in the form of test cases 
     and test outputs, and your explanation of the test is convincing,
     you will get the marks allocated to the feature.  Otherwise you 
     will not get marks for that feature even if you have implemented it. 
   </p>
   <p class="Emphasize"> 
     Read <a href="#docs">Documentation Requirements</a> for further 
     and more detailed requirements regarding the test documentation. 
   </p>
   <p> 
     The project requires a significant amount of work on design and 
     implementation. It is advised that you should start the project
     as soon as possible. 
  </p>

  <h3 id="deadline">Deadline and Penalty for Late Submission 
      (<span class="Back"><a href="#start">Back to Beginning</a></span>) </h3>

  <p>
     The submission deadline of this assignment is specified in
     ICT310 Teaching Schedule page of <a href="../../index.html">
      the Unit Website</a>.
  </p>
  <p>
     Assignments  submitted on or before the deadline will be 
     marked out of 100%. 
  </p>
  <p> Late submission of the assignment will have 5% of the student's raw 
      mark deducted per day, unless an application for extension of submission
      deadline is granted. A submission that is late by more than 10 days 
      or after the last teaching week (Week 14) will not be accepted. 
  </p>
   <p>
     Applications for extension of your assignment deadline can only be made
     via email to the Unit Coordinator, normally prior to
     the specified due date of the assignment.  If an extension is granted
     (also by email), you must attach a copy of the email to your submission
     (see <a href="#docs">Documentation Requirements</a>). Applications 
     for extension by phone or in person do not count,  even if granted.  
     The above policy will be rigorously enforced.
   </p>

  <h3 id="p1"> Project 1: A Simple Unix Shell
      (<span class="Back"><a href="#start">Back to Beginning</a></span>) </h3>
    <p>
       Design and implement a simple UNIX shell program using the grammar
       specified in the <a href="#syntax">later part</a> of this section.
       Please allow for at least 100 commands in a command line and at 
       least 1000 arguments in each command.
    </p>
    <p>
       In addition to the above, the following are required:
     </p>
       <ol>
       <li> <p class="Emphasize"> Reconfigurable shell prompt (default %)</p>  
            <p> The shell must have a shell built-in command <tt>prompt</tt> 
                for changing  the current prompt.  For example, type the 
                following command
            </p>
<pre>
% prompt john$
</pre>
            <p>
                should change the shell prompt to <tt>john$</tt>, i.e., the 
                second  token of the command.
            </p>
       </li>
       <li> <p class="Emphasize">The shell built-in command <code>pwd</code> </p>
            <p> This command prints the current directory (also known as 
                <em>working directory</em>) of the shell process.
            </p>
       </li> 
       <li> <p class="Emphasize">Directory walk</p>
            <p>This command is similar to that provided by the 
               Bash built-in command <tt>cd</tt>. In particular, typing 
               the command without a path should set the current directory 
               of the shell to the home directory of the user.
            </p>
       </li>
       <li> <p class="Emphasize">Wildcard characters</p>
            <p>If a token contains wildcard characters <code>*</code> 
               or <code>?</code> the token is treated as a filename. 
               The wildcard characters in such a token indicate to the 
               shell that the filename must be expanded.  For example 
               the command
            </p>
<pre>
% ls *.c
</pre>
           <p>
               may be expanded to <code>ls ex1.c ex2.c ex3.c </code>if there 
               are three matching files <code>ex1.c ex2.c ex3.c </code> in 
               the current directory.
            </p>
            <p> You may implement this feature using the C function 
               <code>glob</code>.
            </p>
       </li>
       <li> <p class="Emphasize">Standard input and output redirections &gt; and &lt;</p>
            <p> For example:
            </p>
<pre>
% ls -lt &gt;  foo
</pre>
           <p>
               would redirect the standard output of process 
               <tt>ls -lt</tt> to file <tt>foo</tt>.  Similarly in the 
               following command,
            </p>
<pre>
% cat &lt;  foo
</pre>
           <p>
               the standard input of process <tt>cat</tt> is redirected 
               to file <tt>foo</tt>.
            </p>
       </li>
       <li> <p class="Emphasize">Shell pipeline |</p>
           <p>For example: </p>
<pre>
% ls -lt | more
</pre>
         <p>
              the standard output of process <tt>ls -lt</tt>  is connected 
              to the standard input of process <tt>more</tt> via a pipe.
           </p>
       </li>
       <li> <p class="Emphasize">Background job execution</p>
            <p> For example: </p>
<pre>
% xterm &amp;
</pre>
         <p>
               The commannd line starts command <tt>xterm</tt> in the 
               background (ie the shell will not wait for it to terminate
               and you can type in the next command immediately). 
               The following command line
         </p>
<pre>
% sleep 20 &amp;  ps -l
</pre>
         <p>
              starts command  <tt>sleep 20</tt> and immediately execute 
              command <tt>ps -l</tt> without waiting for command 
              <tt>sleep 20</tt> to finish first.
           </p>
       </li>
       <li> <p class="Emphasize">Sequential job execution</p>
            <p> For example the command line
           </p>
<pre>
%  sleep 20 ; ps -l
</pre>
           <p>
               starts command <tt>sleep 20</tt> first, and wait for it 
               to finish, then execute command <tt>ps -l</tt>.
            </p>
       </li>
       <li> <p class="Emphasize">The shell built-in command <code>exit </code></p>
            <p> Use the built-in command <code>exit</code> to terminate
                the shell program.
            </p>
       </li>
       </ol>
      <p> Finally you must not use any existing shell program to 
          implement your shell (for example by calling a shell through 
          the function <code>system</code>).  That would defeat the purpose 
          of this project.
      </p>
      <p> In the above, commands such as <tt>ls</tt>, <tt>cat</tt>, 
          <tt> grep</tt>, <tt>sleep</tt>, <tt>ps</tt> and <tt>xterm</tt>  
          are used as examples to illustrate the use of 
          your shell program. However your shell must be able to handle
          <em>any</em> command or executable program. Note the  commands 
          <tt>prompt</tt>, <tt>pwd</tt>, <tt>cd</tt> and <tt>exit</tt> should be  
          implemented as shell builtins, not as external commands.
      </p>
      <p> The syntax and behaviour of the built-in commands 
          <tt>pwd</tt>, <tt>cd</tt> and <tt> exit</tt> should be similar to the 
          corresponding commands under Bash shell. 
      </p>
      <p> A major part of this shell is a command line parser. 
          Please read the <a href="shell_notes.shtml">this note</a>
          for suggestions on implementing the parser.
      </p>

    <h4 id="syntax"> Definition of Command Line Syntax </h4>
      <p>The following is the formal definition of the command line 
         syntax for the shell, defined in Extended BNF:
      </p>
<pre>
   &lt; command line &gt;      ::=   &lt; job &gt;
                             | &lt; job &gt; '&amp;'
                             | &lt; job &gt; '&amp;' &lt; command line &gt;
                             | &lt; job &gt; ';'
                             | &lt; job &gt; ';' &lt; command line &gt;

   &lt; job &gt;               ::=   &lt; command &gt;
                             | &lt; job &gt; '|' &lt; command &gt;

   &lt; command &gt;           ::=   &lt; simple command &gt;
                             | &lt; simple command &gt; '&lt;' &lt; filename &gt;
                             | &lt; simple command &gt; '&gt;' &lt; filename &gt;

   &lt; simple command &gt;    ::=   &lt; pathname &gt;
                             | &lt; simple command &gt;  &lt; token &gt;
</pre>
      <p>An informal definition plus additional explanations of the 
         syntax is given below: 
        </p>
         <ol>
         <li> <p>A <span class="Emphasize">command line</span>  consists of one 
              or several <span class="Emphasize">jobs</span> separated by the 
              special character "&amp;" and/or ";".  The last <span class="Emphasize">
              job</span> may be followed by the character "&amp;" 
              or ";". If a <span class="Emphasize">job</span> is followed by 
              the character "&amp;", then it should  be executed in background.  
             </p>
         </li>
         <li> <p>A <span class="Emphasize">job</span>  consists of one or more
              <span class="Emphasize">command</span>s separated by pipeline
              characters "|"; 
              </p>
         </li>
         <li> <p>A <span class="Emphasize">command</span> is either a 
              <span class="Emphasize">simple command</span> or a <span class="Emphasize">
              simple command</span> followed by an input redirection
              (&lt; filename) or an output redirection (&gt; filename); 
             </p>
         </li>
         <li> <p>A <span class="Emphasize">simple command</span> consists of a single
              <span class="Emphasize">pathname</span> followed by zero or more tokens; 
              </p>
         </li>
         <li> <p>The following five characters are the <span class="Emphasize">special 
              characters</span>: &amp;, ;, |, &lt; , &gt; ; 
              </p>
         </li>
         <li> <p>The <span class="Emphasize">white space characters</span> are 
              defined to be the space character and the tab character; 
              </p>
         </li>
         <li><p>A <span class="Emphasize">token</span> is either a special character 
              or a string that does not contain space characters or 
              special characters. In this project we do not consider 
              quoted strings. Therefore if single quote or double quote 
              characters appear in a string, they are treated just like 
              any other non-special characters without the usually special
              meaning;
              </p>
         </li>
         <li> <p><span class="Emphasize">Tokens</span> must be separated by one 
              or more white spaces; 
              </p>
         </li>
         <li><p>A <span class="Emphasize">pathname</span> is either a file name, 
             or an absolute pathname, or a relative pathname. Examples of 
             pathnames are <strong>grep</strong>, <strong>/usr/bin/grep</strong>,
             <strong>bin/grep</strong> and <strong>./grep</strong>; 
             </p>
         </li>
         <li> <p>A command line must end with a newline character.
              </p>
         </li>
         </ol>

  <h3 id="p2"> Project 2: A Simple File Transfer Protocol 
      (<span class="Back"><a href="#start">Back to Beginning</a></span>) </h3>
     <p>
        Design and implement a simple network protocol that can be used to
        download files from a remote site and to upload files to a remote
        site, and a client and a server programs that communicate using 
        that protocol.  The protocol should use TCP as its transport 
        layer protocol.  The server must be able to serve multiple client 
        requests simultaneously.  For simplicity, do not consider any 
        authentication process in this project, hence the server will 
        provide its service to any client with the right site address 
        and port number.
     </p>
     <p>
        To simplify project marking, please name your server program
        <tt>myftpd</tt> with the following command line syntax (here the
        letter <tt>d</tt> in <tt>myftpd</tt> stands for daemon, since the 
        server should run as a daemon process:
     </p>
<pre>
myftpd [ initial_current_directory ]
</pre>
     <p>
        The server process maintains a current directory. Its initial
        value should be the one inherited from its parent process
        unless the optional
     </p>
<pre>
initial_current_directory
</pre>
     <p>
        is given. In the latter case, the user supplied path should be
        used to set the initial current directory of the server.
        This can be done using the function <code>chdir</code>.  A client
        can use the <code>cd</code> command to change the (child) server's
        current directory later.
      </p>
      <p>
        The client program should be named <tt>myftp</tt> with the 
        following command line syntax:
      </p>
<pre>
myftp [ hostname | IP_address ]
</pre>
     <p>
        where the optional <tt><i>hostname</i></tt> 
        (<tt><i>IP_address</i></tt>) is the name (address) of the remote 
        host that provides the <tt>myftp</tt> service. If the 
        <tt><i>hostname</i></tt> or <tt><i>IP_address</i></tt> is omitted,
        the local host is assumed.
     </p>
     <p>
        After the connection between the client and the server is
        established, the client should display a prompt <tt>&gt;</tt> 
        and wait for one of the following commands:
     </p>
<ul>
<li> <p><code>pwd</code> - to display the  current directory of the 
        server that is serving the client; </p></li>
<li> <p><code>lpwd</code> - to display the  current directory of 
        the client; </p></li> 
<li> <p><code>dir</code> - to display the file names under the  current 
       directory of the server that is serving the client; </p></li>
<li> <p><code>ldir</code> - to display the file names under the  current 
       directory of the client; </p></li>
<li> <p><code>cd directory_pathname</code>  - to change the current directory
      of the server that is serving the client;</p> </li>
<li> <p><code>lcd directory_pathname</code>  - to change the current directory
      of the client;</p> </li>
<li> <p> <code>get filename </code> - to download the named file from the
       current directory of the  remote server and save
       it in the current directory of the client;</p> </li>
<li> <p> <code>put filename </code> - to upload the named file from the
      current directory of the client to the current
      directory of the remove server. </p> </li>
<li> <p> <code> quit </code> - to terminate the <code> myftp</code> session.</p></li>
</ul>
    <p>
       The <tt>myftp</tt> client should repeatedly display the prompt 
       and wait for a command until the <tt> quit</tt> command is entered.
    </p>
    <p>
      This project consists of three components:
     </p>
<ol>
<li> <p class="Emphasize">Protocol Specification:</p>
     <p> You must specify 
     a protocol for communication between the <tt>myftp</tt> 
     client and the <tt>myftp</tt> server. This protocol will 
     become the <em>sole</em> reference to which the client program 
     and the server program can be separately implemented.  
     This means that, by referring
     to the protocol, the client and server can be implemented
     independent of each other. The design and implementation of
     the client (server) should not depend on (1) what
     strategy and algorithms were used to implement the server
     (client), (2) what programming language were used to implement
     the server (client), and (3) what operating system the server (client)
     is running on. The protocol must be complete,
     i.e.,  it contains all the necessary information required by
     both parties to communicate, such as the format and sequence
     of data exchanges between the client and the server, the
     transport layer protocol (TCP or UDP) used to deliver the
     data, and the server port number.  However it should not
     contain anything that unnecessarily constrains the implementation
     of the client or the server.  For example, there is no point
     to limit the implementation language to a particular programming
     language in the protocol, or to require the client or the server
     to be implemented with a particular data structure.
     </p>
     <p>
     Before you attempt this project, you should first complete 
     the first two exercises in Lab 11. You may also read 
     the Trivial FTP Protocol given in Appendix 17A of the textbook 
     (Stallings: Chapter 17 of Online Chapters). Note TFTP uses UDP, while  
      <tt>myftp</tt> protocol must use TCP.
     </p>
</li>
<li> <p class="Emphasize">Client Program:</p>
     <p>You need to implement a client program according to
     the <tt> myftp</tt> protocol.  Note that the client should 
     never rely on any undocumented internal tricks in the server
     implementation. Apart from the <tt>myftp</tt>  protocol,
     you should not make any other assumption about the server 
     program in your client program.
     </p>
</li>
<li> <p class="Emphasize"> Server Program:</p>
     <p> You need to  implement a server program according to
      the <tt> myftp</tt> protocol.  Note that the server 
      should never rely on any undocumented internal tricks 
      in the client implementation. Apart from the <tt>myftp</tt> 
      protocol,  you should not make any other assumption about 
      the client program in your server program.
    </p>
</li>
</ol>

  <p>Note the following additional requirements/explanations:</p>

<ul>
<li>  <p>The name of the client executable program must be <tt>myftp</tt>.
      The name of the server executable program must be <tt>myftpd</tt>.
      </p>
</li>
<li>  <p> To avoid potential conflict in the use of the server's 
      ``well known'' port number when  several students 
      use the same machine (such as medusa), you should use the 
      <a href="server_ports.pdf"> port </a> allocated to you as the default server listening port.
      </p>
</li>
<li>  <p>Tests should show the cases where both the client and the
      server are on the same machine as well as on different
      machines (you may want to use medusa.murdoch.edu.au to do 
      the testing, however <span class="Emphasize">you must kill your server at 
      the end of the test</span>). They should also show that more
      than one client can obtain the service at the same time.
      You may use the command <tt>script</tt> to record the 
      terminal I/O.  When debugging your network program on 
      a standalone machine (eg, on your home Linux), you may 
      use <tt>localhost</tt> as the ``remote'' host name.
      </p>
</li>
<li>  <p>The specification of the protocol is an important part of
      this question.  Please provide a full specification of the
      protocol in a section separated from the client and server
      implementations. You should complete this specification 
      before starting the implementation of the client and 
      server programs.
      </p>
</li>
</ul>

  <h3 id="p3"> Project 3: A HTTP Client and an HTTP Server 
      (<span class="Back"><a href="#start">Back to Beginning</a></span>) </h3>
     <p>
       This project involves an independent study of an existing 
       protocol named HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol), 
       version 1.0 and version 1.1, and then 
       design and Implement an HTTP client that is able to 
       communicate with any HTTP server, and design and implement
       an HTTP server that is able to provide simple services
       requested by any HTTP client.
     </p>
     <p>Please note that a thorough understanding of the HTTP protocol is
       an important part of this project. Unless you are confident that 
       you are  able to gain a thorough understanding of the protocol, 
       you should not select this project as your assignment.
     </p>
     <p>
       This project has three components:
       </p>
       <ol>
         <li>An essay of between one to two pages long, explaining 
             your understanding of the HTTP protocol.
         </li>
         <li> Design and implementation of an HTTP client program using C,
              see the detailed requirements below.
         </li>
         <li> Design and implementation of an HTTP server program using C, 
              see the detailed requirements below.
         </li>
       </ol>

      <h4>The HTTP Client</h4>
      <p>
         The client program must be able to request resources using 
         the GET method from any HTTP server, such as Apache,
         Microsoft IISi and your own HTTP server. It must also be able
         to handle HEAD and TRACE methods. However it is not required to
         render HTML or any graphics or to manipulate HTML links. 
         Content from an HTTP server can be displayed in the same format 
         as you receive it on the terminal.
      </p>
      <p>
          The client should  be named <tt>myhttp</tt> with the following 
          command line syntax: 
      </p>
<pre>
    myhttp [ -m  <i>&lt;method &gt;</i>  [ -a ]  <i>&lt;url&gt;</i>
</pre>
     <p>
       The command takes an url and send an HTTP request message to 
       the server and receives the response from the server. If there
       is no <tt> -a</tt> option, the program displays the content of
       the response. Otherwise it displays entire response message including
       both the headers and the content. 
      </p>
      <p>By default, the client uses GET method. But if the command line
        include an <tt>-m</tt> option, the client should either use
        HEAD method or TRACE method: If the option is <tt>-m head</tt>, 
        the client should use HEAD method; If the option is <tt>-m trace</tt>, 
        the client should use TRACE method.
      </p>

      <h4>The HTTP Server</h4>

      <p> The server program must be able to perform the following tasks:
        </p>
         <ul>
            <li> serve files or directory listings in response to GET 
                 requests from any HTTP client, such as Mozilla Firefox, 
                 Microsoft Internet as well as your own HTTP client.
            </li>
            <li> handle HEAD method and TRACE method from any client.
            </li> 
            <li> input a MIME type file containing a list of MIME type
                  definition and handle the content accordingly.
            </li>
         </ul>
       <p>
       In addition, your server should run as a daemon and it should 
       be able to serve multiple client requests simultaneously.  
       The server should  be named <tt>myhttpd</tt> with the following 
       command line syntax: 
       </p>
<pre>
    myhttpd [ -p  <i>&lt;port number&gt;</i> ]
            [ -d  <i>&lt;document root&gt;</i> ]
            [ -l  <i>&lt;log file&gt;</i> ]
            [ -m  <i>&lt;file for mime types&gt;</i> ]
            [ -f  <i>&lt;number of preforks&gt;</i> ]
</pre>
      <p> where  </p>
       <ul>
       <li> <p><tt><i>&lt;port number&gt;</i></tt> is an optional port 
            number for the server.  If the optional port number is not 
            supplied, your server should use TCP port 8000. 
            </p>
            <p>
               The default port for HTTP is TCP 80. However on Unix, 
               only the root can use ports that are below 1024. 
               To run your server with port 80, you must logon as the 
               root (which is not possible in some machines such as
               medusa.murdoch.edu.au). This is the reason we use 
               port 8000 instead of 80 as the default port.
            </p>
            <p>When testing your server on a shared machine such as
               medusa, you should avoid using port 8000, as there may
               be clashes if two students use the same port at the same 
               time on that machine.  To avoid potential conflict 
               you should use the <a href="server_ports.pdf"> port </a> 
               allocated to you to test your server.
            </p></li>
       <li> <p><tt><i>&lt;document root&gt;</i></tt> is an optional
            directory path representing the document root of the server
            under which all files are stored. Without this option, 
            you document root is taken as the current directory of the
            server.
            </p>
            <p> When testing your server, make sure that under your
               document root, there are regular files as well as 
               directories. Some of these directories contains 
               the index file <tt>index.html</tt>. Other directories 
               do not contain this index file.  Your should test 
               both cases.
            </p></li> 
       <li> <p><tt><i>&lt;log file&gt;</i></tt> is an optional path of
            the log file, to which the server will send its logs. 
            Without this option, your log file should be 
            <tt>./myhttdp.log</tt>, ie file <tt>myhttpd.log</tt> 
            under the server's current directory.
            </p>
            <p>Your server must add one line into the log file for 
               each client request, giving the date and time of the 
               request, the HTTP method in the request, the originating 
               host, the resource request and status code returned
               to the client.
            </p></li> 
       <li> <p><tt><i>&lt;file for mime types&gt;</i></tt> is an optional
            file containing a list of mime types that the server 
            recognises. Without this option, your server would only
            recognise the following mime types:
               <tt>text/plain</tt>, <tt>text/html</tt>, <tt>image/jpeg</tt>, 
               and <tt>image/gif</tt>. 
            </p>
            <p>In testing your server, you must at least test the above
               file types plus two additional file types.
            </p></li>
       <li> <p><tt><i>&lt;number of preforks&gt;</i></tt> is an optional
            number of preforks. Without this option, the number of
            preforks is fixed at 5. 
            </p>
            <p>Preforks mean that the server
            (parent server) will always maintain a pool of idle child 
            processes (child servers), so that when a client request 
            arrives, the parent server can immediately hand it to one 
            of the idle child servers. In this way the client can get 
            speedier service rather than waiting for the parent server 
            to create a new child process before it can be served. 
            Note that it takes a long time to create new  child process.
            </p>
            <p>It is not a trivial task to design an efficient web server 
               that can serve many client requests simultaneously and 
               quickly. You may want to consider using <tt>clone</tt>
               systems call to create child processes to reduce the 
               overhead. However if you choose to do so, you must be
               careful with the global variables as they are shared 
               between the parent and all child processes! 
            </p></li>
       </ul>
       <p>Please note that the server <tt>myhttpd</tt> can take any combination
          of the above five command line options, not necessarily one option
          each time. For example, we may run the server with two options
          as shown below:
       </p>
<pre>
%  myhttpd  -p 12345  -l /tmp/hong.log
</pre>
       <p>In addition to the above requirements, your server must be able
          list file names in a directory if the URL points to a directory
          on the server and that directory does not contain an index file
          (<tt>index.html</tt>).
       </p>
       <p>
         To complete this project you will have to carry out research on
         issues such as web server, HTTP protocol, MIME type, etc.  
         There are numerous Internet sites providing the 
         relevant materials.  A good starting point is 
         <a href="http://en.wikipedia.org">Wikipedia</a>.
       </p>

<h3 id="docs"> Documentation Requirements 
      (<span class="Back"><a href="#start">Back to Beginning</a></span>) </h3>
     <p>
         Your assignment must be submitted in the form of a single tar
